title: Soft preemption and spread-shed strategy for hosted GPU backlog stabilization
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the Jan-Feb hosted API saturation window we observed repeatable queue buildup driven by tenant-level burst patterns and a small number of long-running sampling workloads. Existing hard-throttle eviction created cascading retries and amplified queue pressure. This ticket defines a complementary set of runtime changes we will deliver as the primary mitigation: soft preemption, spread-shed admission, and tenant-aware hysteresis to smooth transient spikes while preserving fairness and latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce observed 95/99th tail latency during pool surge events by preventing queue amplification.
- Avoid wholesale eviction of tenant work; instead preempt low-priority fragments and spread remaining load across available nodes.
- Provide transparent metrics and an operator runbook to safely rollback changes if unintended regressions appear.

Scope of work (high-level):
1) Soft preemption: implement a mechanism that marks low-impact in-flight requests as "soft-preemptable" at admission time (configurable TTL). On congestion, these requests are signaled to upstream SDKs (via 202+ Retry-After semantics) to gracefully pause rather than fully evict or block higher-priority traffic. This reduces burst amplification caused by clients immediately reissuing full-size requests.

2) Spread-shed admission policy: instead of per-pool FIFO shed, implement per-tenant spread scoring that spreads shed decisions across nodes and tenants to reduce pooling hotspots. The scoring uses recent token-rate, historical SLA tier, and active-kv-cache-fraction to compute a normalized admission score.

3) Tenant-aware hysteresis and cooldown: add a moving-window hysteresis so a tenant that was recently shed slowly regains admission capacity (exponential backoff with jitter), avoiding oscillation loops that caused repeated thrashing in prior incidents.

4) Ephemeral burst nodes + prewarm hints: enable a small ring of ephemeral instances that can be primed for very short lived bursts. These nodes are instrumented with KV-cache warm hints propagated by the admission layer to reduce cold-start penalty for common prefix patterns.

5) Observability and safety: ship dashboards with admission score distributions, soft-preempt counts, per-tenant shed rate, and synthetic-surge Canary jobs. Add feature flag gating and per-region kill-switch in Console for fast rollback.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Patel: Filed after postmortem call with oncall and runtime leads. Root cause: tenant burst + long tail workload causing queue amplification when hard-evict policy returned many tokens to the admission window. Recommended soft preemption as least-regressive path.

2025-02-20 - Jonah Reyes: Design review completed. Decided to implement soft-preempt as an admission-time token annotation + short lived preempt queue rather than modifying kernel eviction. Added requirement: SDKs should honor 202/Retry-After semantics for graceful pause (SDK change tracked in ENG-33168).

2025-02-24 - Nick Huang (runtime): Prototype of admission-score computed. Initial formula: score = (recent_tokens / 95th_historical_tokens) * tier_penalty * (1 - kv_cache_fill). Observed better spread across nodes in local sim. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2891

2025-02-27 - Ops: Canary run in us-west-2 with traffic replay from 2025-01-23 incident window. Soft-preempt reduced reissue amplification by ~42% and dropped 99th tail token latency by 18%. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinfra.com/d/hosted/gpu-admission?orgId=1&panelId=7

2025-03-01 - PM review (Lena Ortiz): Confirmed scope and approved user-visible telemetry fields. Added requirement to include per-tenant shed reason codes for customer support and billing reconciliation.

2025-03-03 - Security: Light review completed, no secrets introduced. Noted KMS calls from ephemeral nodes must be scoped to read-only model metadata roles. Recorded in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RE/ENG-33123+soft-preempt

2025-03-04 - Jonah Reyes: Split implementation into three PRs: admission-core, SDK-backpressure, and canary-job. admission-core PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2928. Added automated load test for tenant fairness. Estimate adjusted to 8 points.

2025-03-05 - Oncall: Add runbook entry under hosted-capacity-runbooks: step 1 toggle feature flag to 'soft-preempt-v1', step 2 monitor per-tenant shed rate and 95/99 latency; step 3 rollback if customer-facing 5xx increase >0.5% over baseline.
